text: plan-defect: the fifth GLOBAL CONSTRAINT states the block is "under 24 KB however many failures the run recorded", but the only quantities bounded are the row count (FACTS_MAX_ROWS = 20, fleet/facts-block.mjs:77,142) and each evidence field (FACTS_FIELD_MAX = 500, fleet/facts-block.mjs:80,105-108). rowLine (fleet/facts-block.mjs:117) renders `row.paths.join(', ')` — the row's entire path list, unbounded in count and length. At the bound, 20 rows already spend ~20,000 characters on read+against plus ~1.6 KB of fixed per-row text and ~200 characters of header, leaving under ~2 KB for every path of every row. A `driver:finding` whose detail names no path carries the task's whole touch set (Task 3 M1), so a many-file task can push a single row's path join past that alone and the block over 24 KB. The fix is not available inside this task's FILES: M2 spells the row line as `[<paths joined by ', '>]` — the row's own paths, all of them, which is also the reading the exam pins byte-for-byte at fleet/tests/test_facts_block.mjs:452-463 — so capping the rendered list here would contradict the Machine clause the diff was graded on. Settling it means amending M2 (a per-row path budget, or a tail elision) or restating the constraint's arithmetic to bound only the evidence fields. Nothing in this submission is wrong against its own task text
recording it so the operator can decide before Task 5 wires the block into a brief.

concern: out-of-FILES (not taken): fleet/CONTRACT.md — the Global Constraint says every new event field is named there, and `paths`/`evidence` on `driver:wave-blocked` and `driver:publish-fold` are new fields. The path is Task 6's (popmechanic-ultrapowers#1csr), so the contract sentences for those two kinds still owe both keys.

Code quality, `examReceiptOf` in `fleet/run-engine.mjs`: `paths` is built as `[...landings, ...files].map(String).filter(Boolean)`, so the `String` conversion runs *before* the truthiness filter. `landingOf` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:2488) returns `undefined` whenever a factsheet is present and its `landing` map has no entry for a Proof path — `String(undefined)` is the non-empty string `'undefined'`, which survives `.filter(Boolean)` and lands in the record as a repo-relative path that does not exist. Filtering first also keeps the Context slot's shared literal honest on the other edge (`paths` "never empty"): with both lists empty the current code silently yields `[]`. Neither case is reachable in the sims (leg (b)'s task has no factsheet and `examRunnable` requires `proofTests.length`), so the exam is green either way — this is a defensive one-liner, not a failing leg.

concern: out-of-FILES (not taken): fleet/CONTRACT.md — the Global Constraint "Every new event kind and every new event field is named in fleet/CONTRACT.md" is now owed two entries this task's code created: the `paths` and `evidence` fields on `driver:exam-run`, and the fact that `resolver:reply` is a row the wave loop actually writes (the contract lists the kind only among those the status projection skips). fleet/CONTRACT.md is Task 6's declared file, so the edit was not mine to land.

`renderedReceiptIds` is added as a module-level `export` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1286) but nothing imports it — the only caller is `factsFor` a few hundred lines below, in the same module. The task's Interfaces name exactly one Produces symbol, `waveContendingBlock`

exporting a second helper widens the engine's public surface past what the task declares, and past what either Proof `Test:` path pins (`test_resolver_brief.mjs` asserts only `waveContendingBlock`). Dropping the `export` keeps the Produces contract the one the task named.

The wave loop's `contendingBlock` wrapper (fleet/run-engine.mjs:4066-4075) renders the block once via `blockForConflict(conflict)` and then asks `factsFor` for the same query a second time, re-deriving the conflict path with a second copy of `String((conflict && conflict.path) || '')` — the same expression `waveContendingBlock` already carries at line 50 of the patch. The comment argues the two answers cannot differ, which is true today, but it is two spellings of one path rule and two renders of one block

if either side's path derivation is ever changed the `driver:facts` row would silently name rows the resolver never read. The block the wrapper already holds is enough: `if (block) appendEvent({ kind: 'driver:facts', label: 'resolve:wave' + waveNumber + ':' + conflict.i, receipts: renderedReceiptIds(block) })` records exactly the rendered rows without a second query, which is the same invariant `factsFor` was built to hold for the examiner and reviewer.

`renderedReceiptIds` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1286-1293) recovers ids by splitting the rendered block on `\n` and matching `/^- receipt (\S+) /` per physical line, but `factsBlock`'s `field()` bounds a receipt's `read`/`against` to 500 characters without stripping newlines, and two receipt kinds put freeform worker text there — `resolverReceiptOf` renders a resolver's `notes` into `read`, and `driver:finding` renders a review block's `detail`. A receipt whose evidence text happens to contain a line beginning `- receipt <token> ` would put a phantom id into the `driver:facts` row's `receipts`, which is the array the operator's pre-registered reading is counted from. This is record-row noise only — the judge's own brief is unaffected — but anchoring the match to the full row shape (id, kind and the `[` that opens the paths list, e.g. `/^- receipt (\S+) \S+ \[/`) removes the class.
